skill.name: fable-mode
skill.description: Portable five-gate working discipline for pi, OpenCode, and Claude. The backbone that routes to the specialist skills.

automatic_when: debugging where the first theory might be wrong
work is too big for one context window

references.note: Full text of every skill in this repo, embedded so fable-mode is self-contained. Load with read when the standalone skill is not installed. Generated by scripts/sync-references.sh — do not edit by hand.

routes.pattern: blocked on a fact nobody wrote down
blocked on a fact only code can answer
out of context or forking a session

specialist_flow_routing.fallback: Apply the five gates and the inline guidance in SKILL.md.

code_smell_baseline._comment: Used when reviewing and the repo documents no standards of its own. Repo standards override these. Each is a judgement call, not a violation. Skip anything tooling already enforces.

smells.name: Mysterious Name
smells.what: you had to read the body to learn what it does
smells.fix: rename; if no honest name exists, the design is murky

smells.name: Duplicated Code
smells.what: the same decision is made in two places
smells.fix: extract the shared shape; they will drift otherwise

smells.name: Feature Envy
smells.what: a method spends its life in another object's data
smells.fix: move it onto the data it envies

smells.name: Data Clumps
smells.what: the same few params always travel together
smells.fix: they are one concept; give it a name

smells.name: Primitive Obsession
smells.what: a string that is really an email, a number that is really cents
smells.fix: give the concept its own small type

smells.name: Repeated Switches
smells.what: the same switch on the same type recurs

smells.name: Shotgun Surgery
smells.what: one conceptual change forces edits in seven files
smells.fix: the concept has no home; give it one

smells.name: Divergent Change
smells.what: one file is edited for seven unrelated reasons
smells.fix: split so each module changes for one reason

smells.name: Speculative Generality
smells.what: an abstraction, hook, or flag with exactly one caller
smells.fix: delete it and the branch it guards

smells.name: Message Chains
smells.what: a.b().c().d() — the caller now knows the object graph
smells.fix: hide the walk behind one method

smells.name: Middle Man
smells.what: a class that only forwards calls
smells.fix: cut it; call the real target

smells.name: Refused Bequest
smells.what: an implementation that throws on half its interface

debugging.two_strike_rule: Two failed fixes for the same bug means the diagnosis is wrong, not incomplete. Stop patching.

axes.name: Spec
axes.question: Does the change do what was asked? What is missing, partial, extra, or simply wrong?

axes.name: Standards
axes.question: Is this code we want to keep? Repo standards first; smell baseline only if there are none.

model_recommendations._comment: Model IDs use OpenCode / OpenCode Go conventions. For pi or Claude, map these to your harness's provider/model syntax.

sub_agent_reviewer.description: Read-only review, security or performance audit

sub_agent_test_runner.description: Running tests, parsing output, reporting failures

overall_best_balance.reason: Strong coding performance with reliable tool calling; priced between budget and flagship open models.

best_cost_benefit.reason: Very cheap and allows a high request ceiling per window on the Go plan; good for bulk or iterative work.

best_quality_open_model.reason: Top-tier open coding model, comparable to proprietary mid-range for many tasks.

best_for_sub_agents.reason: Good tool use, large context, low enough cost to run several in parallel.

spawn_when: a test or debug loop can be isolated
the task has clearly separable workstreams
sub_agent_config.default_prompt_prefix: You are a sub-agent running the Fable Method. Pass through all five gates. Do not modify files unless explicitly permitted. Report verified facts and assumptions separately.

fable-reviewer.prompt: Run the Fable Method. Gate 1: confirm scope. Gate 2: read the actual files. Gate 3: attack your own findings. Gate 4: verify by re-reading. Gate 5: report verified vs assumed, Spec and Standards separately. Do not edit files.
